reviews.title: Solid pick
reviews.comment: Needed to upgrade the power supply in my PC to accommodate a larger graphics card. For the price, this is an excellent pick, and I appreciate my friend for recommending it. Installation was dead simple with a couple of screws to get it into place in my case, and the connectors included more than I could ever need. No annoying buzz, and it powers my PC just as I expected. This is not modular, which means the cable management is not as easy as it could be, but it's a fair trade-off for a significantly lower price.
reviews.author: Alex

reviews.title: Great PSU
reviews.comment: First thing I'll mention is that I received a used/returned unit, which was very obvious.  Everything was there and other than a label that was slightly peeling, it was a fully functioning working unit.  I can't blame manufacturers for reselling all the stuff that's RMA'd due to inexperienced computer builders. I've used at least 3 of these in recent builds and all continue to work well after 9+ months.  Only complaint is that some motherboards have two 12V EPS connectors (CPU) and this PSU only has one.  In practice it makes no difference because most motherboard/CPU combos don't need the second connector, but it would be nice to have the second one installed. I love the sleeved multi-colored & ketchup/mustard wiring, it makes diagnosing PCs so much easier.  Nothing worse than diagnosing all black wiring and having to look up connector pinouts to see which one is which.  I use these PSUs for customers, and I don't like modular wiring because they might need to add something in the future, which in that case you'd have to leave the extra wires connected anyways for that purpose. I used to buy another brand for these types of builds (obviously these aren't high end gaming systems) that is no longer available, but this has been a great alternative for the price and has a gold efficiency rating.  Zero complaints so far, and very quiet while in use.
reviews.author: Ashley Warren

reviews.title: Thermaltake Toughpower gold 600W SLI/Crossfire Ready work great. Work on an ASUS Motherboard. A+
reviews.comment: I needed a new power supply. I put it in and it works great. The fan is quiet. Eventing works an usual. I had an old Corsiar power supply and it wasn't working like it should. It was whining and the fan wasn't working to well. This new power supply is great and it has a 5 year warranty. A+
reviews.author: Vassilis Kitsos

reviews.title: Great on a budget, with a catch.
reviews.comment: If you're looking to build a budget PC, this thing is a pretty sweet deal (in the $50-$60 range). Just keep in mind, the two 6+2 pin power connectors are daisy-chained, so there is only 1 cable's worth of power. If your GPU will draw 275+ watts, you might consider something else. Other than that, it's a pretty great power supply.
reviews.author: AmazonUser

reviews.title: Reliable PSU
reviews.comment: PSU has good quality, it runs quiet, and had every connector I needed for my gtx1080 and mobo etc. looks great with my build, I couldn't be happier with thermal take with this one.
